newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Tyndall unaware of reasons for rise.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Tyndall unaware of reasons for rise.

text.p: Funds manager, Tyndall Australia Ltd said on Wednesday it was unaware of any reason for the increase in its share price or the volume of its shares traded since November 20, other than normal market forces.
Responding to a price query from the Australian Stock Exchange, Tyndall said there were no matters of importance concerning the company which required an announcement to be made to the market.
In a letter to Tyndall dated November 26, the ASX said between November 20 and November 26, Tyndall shares rose 17 cents to A$2.02 and there was a noticeable increase in volume.

"The company continues to receive favourable press comments in relation to its funds management performance and from its recent announcement of its in-principle agreement to acquire all the issued capital of Oceanic Capital Holdings Ltd," Tyndall said in its letter of response.
Tyndall announced on October 24 that it had agreed in principle to acquire Oceanic for A$40 million.

Oceanic was owned by Financial Insurance Fund L.P., a United States-based group of insurers and reinsurers, which owned the company for five years after purchasing it from the debt-ridden State Bank of South Australia.
Oceanic has funds under management of A$250 million, and will bring Tyndall's total funds under management to A$6.3 billion.
Tyndall, which is 51 percent owned by Guinness Peat Group Plc, said the purchase price would include a mixture of cash and the issue of medium term convertible debt.
Tyndall shares were 0.9 cents lower at A$2.041 at 10.45 a.m. (2345 GMT).
